title: Audit of Data Contamination and Construct Validity in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: How prevalent are dataset contamination and construct-invalidity issues in selected public LLM-for-NetOps benchmarks, and how much does applying preregistered contamination controls plus realism adjustments reduce measured model success rates?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A measurable fraction of benchmark items will be flagged as probable contamination by preregistered deterministic heuristics (exact fingerprint + fuzzy n-gram overlap + metadata provenance), producing nonzero contamination rates per dataset.

H2: The paired success-rate difference (guarded_minus_baseline) across items and models will be negative (performance decreases) and detectably different from zero under the paired_binary_analysis_v1 estimand when comparing baseline items to contamination-controlled + realism-adjusted variants.
H3: Items classified as "templated/low-complexity" by an automated templating detector will show larger paired success-rate drops than items classified as "realistic/high-complexity".
exploratory_questions: E1: How contamination-flag prevalence varies by dataset provenance (OpenAlex/DOI source) and by simple vs complex NetOps task classes?
E2: How sensitive the paired effect is to the fuzzy-overlap threshold (sensitivity curve).
model_scope: Hosted LLM APIs (up to 4 models in recommended scenario). Exact model identifiers will be recorded in execution manifest; hosted_model_api_available per capability manifest.
transformation_scope: Controlled contamination removal/holdout (deterministic exclusion of flagged items).
Realism adjustments implemented deterministically: vendor retemplating (token-level template substitution), and topology-complexity augmentation (parameterized synthetic augmentation).
secondary_estimands: contamination_rate_per_dataset (proportion of items flagged by heuristics)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample units are item × model pairs, paired across baseline vs guarded variants. Datasets: 3 public datasets selected above. Item selection: random deterministic seed sampling from each dataset (seed published). Item counts and model counts are determined by budget scenario. For the recommended scenario: 150 items total (50 items per dataset) × 4 models = 600 item-model pairs. Each pair is evaluated on two variants (baseline and guarded), yielding 600 pairs for the paired analysis (paired within the same item-model pair comparing baseline vs guarded). Model-call arithmetic: 150 items × 4 models × 2 variants = 1,200 model calls. All sampling uses fixed random seed(s) and published sampling script hashes.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis uses registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' with estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Each item-model pair yields binary success/failure determined by deterministic validators: (a) for config/intent tasks: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 verifier checks property correctness (reachability/policy); (b) for templated-answer tasks: exact-match or normalized canonicalization comparator. The analysis executor will run the primary analysis (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analysis will include complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity. Stratified analyses by templated vs realistic items will be reported. All code, seeds, and result artifacts will be published with hashes.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory estimand is the paired difference aggregated across all item-model pairs. Secondary stratified analyses (templated vs realistic) are explicitly prespecified. Reported p-values will be two-sided and multiplicity for secondary analyses will be controlled by reporting effect sizes and 95% CIs rather than uncorrected multiple p-value claims. Primary hypothesis H2 is single prespecified test.
missingness_plan: If a model/API call fails, follow analysis contract failed_call_treatment: first attempt retries per preregistered retry policy (one retry within 5 minutes). If still failing, treat the pair per registered executor options (complete_pair_primary or sensitivity variant). All failed-call counts and causes logged and reported.

risk_factors: Public availability of near-identical items in web-crawled corpora used by hosted LLMs
Templated task phrasing leading to memorized outputs
Dataset provenance timestamps predating model training cutoffs (probabilistic overlap)
detection_procedures: Exact-match fingerprinting: normalize whitespace and canonicalize tokens; flag exact duplicates between dataset item text and collected public corpus fingerprints.

Fuzzy n-gram overlap: compute jaccard/overlap over 5-gram shingles between item and public-corpus document set; preregistered thresholds: flag if overlap ≥ 0.80 (high-confidence) or ≥ 0.50 (low-confidence).

Metadata provenance tracing: compare dataset item timestamps and explicit source DOIs/URLs to known public artifacts (using supplied evidence record IDs) and flag likely pretraining-era items when source timestamp < model-public-cutoff (model cutoff metadata recorded).
item_flagging_rules: High-confidence contamination flag if exact-match OR fuzzy 5-gram overlap ≥ 0.80.
Medium-confidence flag if fuzzy overlap in [0.50,0.80) OR provenance timestamp strongly predates model cutoff and source matches public archive.
Low-confidence flags recorded but not removed in the baseline cleaning unless sensitivity analysis indicates otherwise.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Guarded variant (for confirmatory comparison) excludes high-confidence flagged items deterministically (holdout) and replaces them with synthetically retemplated items sampled from the same dataset distribution (deterministic augmentation seeds). Realism adjustments (vendor retemplating + topology complexity augmentation) are applied to the held-out items to create guarded variants. The paired comparison uses the same item identifiers where possible (original vs guarded replacement) and pairs are aligned deterministically.
residual_uncertainty: Overlap inferences remain probabilistic without authoritative training-corpus manifests; contamination flags are heuristic estimates.
Fuzzy-overlap thresholds induce tradeoffs between false positives and false negatives; sensitivity curves will be reported.

budget_scenarios.description: Low-cost audit for initial signal detection.
transformations: vendor retemplating applied to removed items
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 100 items total (≈33 per dataset) × 2 models × 2 variants = 400 model calls. Arithmetic: items (100) × models (2) × variants (2) = 400.

budget_scenarios.description: Balanced power and feasible model-call budget matching earlier estimate.
transformations: high- and medium-confidence flag removal (exact-match and fuzzy ≥0.50) with synthetic retemplating
vendor retemplating and topology-complexity augmentation for realism-adjusted replacements
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 150 items total (50 per dataset) × 4 models × 2 variants = 1,200 model calls. Arithmetic: items (150) × models (4) × variants (2) = 1,200.

budget_scenarios.description: Larger cross-model audit and extended sensitivity sweeps.
transformations: full-flag removal and multi-variant realism augmentations
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 200 items × 6 models × 2 variants = 2,400 model calls. Arithmetic: items (200) × models (6) × variants (2) = 2,400. Still under capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10,000).

power_plan.target_effect: Detect a 5 percentage-point absolute decrease in success rate (0.05) with 80% power at α=0.05
power_plan.clustering_unit: item × model pair (paired across baseline vs guarded variants)
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal approximation for paired proportion differences (two-sided); conservative assumed baseline success rate 0.60 for planning; intraclass dependence addressed by pairing; calculations produce required number of pairs (item-model pairs).
assumptions: Within-pair correlation moderate (ρ ≈ 0.4); paired design reduces variance versus unpaired
Planned confirmatory pairs from recommended scenario = 150 items × 4 models = 600 pairs
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With 600 paired trials, assuming baseline 0.60 and within-pair correlation 0.4, detectable absolute paired difference ≈ 0.04–0.06 (approx); sensitivity analysis will sweep baseline rates 0.4–0.8 and correlations 0.2–0.6.
sensitivity_analyses: Vary fuzzy-overlap thresholds (0.50, 0.65, 0.80) and report effect size changes.
Vary assumed baseline success rate in power post-hoc explanation (0.4,0.6,0.8).

transformation_families: Exact removal (holdout) of flagged items and deterministic synthetic retemplating replacements.
Vendor retemplating: deterministic template substitution mapping vendor X->vendor Y using canonical token mapping rules.
Topology-complexity augmentation: parameterized deterministic addition of intermediate nodes/links to increase path diversity.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated intent-preservation comparator: compare original vs transformed item intent embedding cosine similarity (threshold preregistered at ≥0.85) using hosted-model-API embeddings; reject transformation if similarity < threshold.

Functional check: run hosted_netops_gvr_v1 validator on transformed config and ensure that the functional property class (e.g., intended connectivity) differs only as intended for realism adjustments; automatic rejection if property mismatches indicate semantic drift beyond prespecified delta.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject transformed item if intent-preservation embedding similarity < 0.85.
Reject and re-generate (deterministic reparameterization) if verifier indicates unintended property regressions (not the controlled realism augmentation).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated audit uses synthetic-ground-truth injection for estimating heuristic FP/FN rates: deterministic duplicates and synthetic contamination examples are injected into a held-out synthetic corpus to measure detection heuristic performance. All audit steps are reproducible scripts with fixed seeds; no human annotation is used.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: All retemplating and augmentation code is unit-tested with deterministic fixtures; hashes of transformation code and fixtures will be published before execution.
residual_risks: Embedding-based intent preservation is an imperfect proxy and may misclassify semantic drift.
Synthetic retemplating may not perfectly capture production vendor diversity; results should be interpreted within the declared dataset scope.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Definitive attribution of contamination to proprietary LLM training corpora remains probabilistic because authoritative training manifests are unavailable (evidence: selection unresolved_uncertainties).
Heuristic contamination detection has residual false-positive/false-negative risk despite synthetic audit; reported rates will reflect those uncertainties.

Realism adjustments via deterministic retemplating and synthetic augmentation may not capture all real-world vendor idiosyncrasies; external generalization is limited to the declared public dataset scope.
Legal/reputational sensitivity of provenance claims: we will redact item-level provenance and publish only aggregated statistics and sanitized examples per our conservative disclosure policy.
